overall_reason: The page has no real chart; its figures are KPI confetti: a looping hero row of six baseline-free claims ('98% faster deployment', '300% throughput increase', '6x faster to ship') and a 'Live metrics' block with a ticking clock over four tiles on four different periods.

score.reason: T-STAT-TILE fails on the hero row and the live-metrics block (no baseline, mixed periods, a staged live counter), and T-FILLER fails on the repeated 99.99% uptime tiles (DVZ-013, DVZ-003, DVZ-001).

findings.where: hero stat row, section.relative.min-h-screen > div.absolute.bottom-12 > div.flex.gap-16, 1440, contact sheet #10, tiles/1440-00.png
findings.evidence: The first screen ends in a row of 48px figures: '98% faster deployment STRIPE', '300% throughput increase LINEAR', '6x faster to ship NOTION', '20 days saved on builds NETFLIX', then '98%' and '300%' again (stat_tiles row_size 6; the row is duplicated for a marquee loop). No tile says faster or more than what, over what period, or for which workload. The row mixes percent, multiplier and days.
findings.before: Six 48px figures with a word and a brand name each, no baseline and no period, repeated in a loop.
findings.after: One sourced figure with its baseline and period, for example 'Deploys went from [DATA NEEDED: before time] to [DATA NEEDED: after time] at Stripe, Q1 2026', or cut the row.
findings.why: A percentage with no baseline cannot be checked or compared, and three different units in one row stop a reader comparing the tiles at all. Whether the claims are real is lens-integrity's (the sweep's INT-001 and INT-007 hits are on the same row).
findings.root: one stat-tile component without a baseline or period field, used in the hero row and the infrastructure row

findings.where: 'Performance you can measure.' section, div.grid.grid-cols-1 > div.bg-background.p-8 (four tiles), 1440, contact sheet #4 to #7, tiles/1440-05.png
findings.evidence: A green dot and 'Live | 1:08:57 AM' sit beside four 96px tiles: '2,847,392 API requests today', '99.99% Uptime this quarter', '23ms Average response time' and '184 Countries served'. The four tiles use four periods (today, this quarter, none, none) and four units, and none carries a trend or comparison.
findings.before: A 'Live metrics' block whose only live element is a clock, over four unrelated figures on different periods.
findings.after: Keep one figure the visitor can act on, for example '23ms median API response, last 30 days', with a link to the status page, and drop the clock and the 'Live' dot.
findings.why: A ticking clock next to static figures stages a live dashboard on a marketing page; the reader is asked to trust the label 'Live' rather than shown data.

findings.where: infrastructure tiles (tiles/1440-04.png, contact sheet #8, #9) and live-metrics tiles (tiles/1440-05.png, #5)
findings.evidence: The page shows 99.99% uptime as a tile three times: 'Uptime SLA' in the infrastructure row, 'Uptime this quarter' in the live block, and again in the security copy (sweep invented_metrics hits on '99.99% uptime' at three selectors). The infrastructure row's '<50ms Global latency' repeats the sentence beside it ('delivering sub-50ms latency to 99% of the world').
findings.before: The same figure restated as a big tile in three sections, and a tile that repeats the paragraph next to it.
findings.after: Show uptime once, with its period and a link to a status history, and let the edge-network list carry the latency (it already lists 12ms to 45ms per region).
findings.why: Repeating one figure in three places adds no information and makes each tile look like filler.

strengths: The 'Edge Network' list (tiles/1440-04.png) gives one latency per named region (San Francisco 12ms to Sydney 45ms), right-aligned in a monospaced face; it backs the '<50ms' claim better than the tile does.
The live-metrics tiles carry worded qualifiers under each figure ('API requests today', 'Uptime this quarter').
not_investigated: the data behind each chart: the capture cannot see it, so only what the page shows is judged
tooltips, hover values and keyboard access to data points
charts inside tabs, carousels or menus the capture did not open
charts that animate in: each screenshot is one moment
canvas internals: canvas regions were read from their crops only
whether a source line points to a real source (lens-integrity's)
visitor mode inferred as Persuade (a SaaS landing page with 'Start free trial'); there is no 00-contract.md

the two large canvases (hero, 800 by 800px, contact #2; pricing, 500 by 500px, contact #3) and the footer canvas are generative line-glyph art, not charts; the svg the table lists as a chart (contact #1, 192 by 160px) is a document icon with six text lines
whether the figures are true or attributed with permission to Stripe, Linear, Notion and Netflix: lens-integrity's (INT-001, INT-007 already in the sweep)
